text:
anya: Quick thread to reconcile the intake vs heavy-bench tradeoffs after yesterday's call. I'm leaning to 'accept-light, verify-heavy' model: accept on fast checks then gate traffic via canary until async bench finishes. Pros/cons?

raj: That matches my thinking. Main downside: time window where a model is partially live. We should minimize blast radius with strict canary rules and automatic rollback triggers. Also need explicit lifecycle states so tooling can reason about candidates.

kevin: Suggest states: pending_ingest, light_accepted, verifying_async, live_canary, promoted, quarantined, rejected. Each state should have allowed transitions and TTLs. Example: light_accepted -> verifying_async (if bench scheduled) or -> rejected (if intake failed). verifying_async -> promoted OR quarantined.

liz: For intake checks keep them tiny: tokenizer roundtrip, shape/boolean ops, a couple of synthetic prompts to catch EOS/pad bugs, and a micro-latency check (single forward pass). These should be <30s. Heavy bench runs the full golden/regression suite, distributional evals, latency percentiles, and quality metrics (e.g., rouge/qa-accuracy).

anya: How do we coordinate golden sets? If intake uses a small probe and bench uses a larger golden, we must track which golden_set was used. Let's add golden_set_id to the model metadata and to the bench results. Runtime should reject models whose golden_set_id is missing or mismatched.

raj: Operational controls: - Max concurrent bench jobs per org - Max GPU-hours/day quota - Pending timeout (if bench result missing after X hours, mark as "stale" and require manual review) - Priority queueing (enterprise customers first).

kevin: Also: if bench flags a model as quarantined, we should automatically (a) remove it from routing, (b) mark any recent promotions and associated canaries for rollback, and (c) create an incident ticket with attached failed test artifacts.

liz: For rollout recipe: 1) light_accepted -> run shadow traffic for 24h, gather real-world latencies but don't route responses. 2) live_canary: route 0.1% traffic for 2 hours. If no regressions, 3) ramp to 1%, then 5%, then full. Bench results can veto at any step.

bench-bot: Bench job created: candidate=ingest-2026-03-26-9, est_gpu_hours=4.2, expected_done=~8h. Webhook target=/intake/hooks/bench-result.

anya: API sketch for bench result webhook (payload keys only): candidate_id, status (passed|flagged|critical), failed_checks (list), drift_metric (float), p95_latency_ms, golden_set_id, bench_run_id, artifacts_url. Example payload:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "ingest-2026-03-26-9",
  "status": "flagged",
  "failed_checks": ["regression:qa_suite_v4", "embedding_cosine_drop"],
  "drift_metric": "0.21",
  "p95_latency_ms": "280",
  "golden_set_id": "gold-2026-03-01-a1",
  "bench_run_id": "bench-9876",
  "artifacts_url": "https://bench.internal/runs/bench-9876"
}
```

raj: Make sure the webhook includes a small verdict enum (accept/flag/quarantine) plus a human-readable reason. Also include minimal diffs (summary) to avoid loading huge artifacts into the webhook.

kevin: We should cap async spend per org and surface current usage in the console. If an org is near quota, intake should degrade to require manual approval for new models. Also consider a cheap prefilter that runs a few golden prompts to avoid wasting bench cycles on obviously incompatible models.

liz: Edgecases: - Tokenizer drift where same prompt tokenizes differently across model versions. Fast-probe should include tokenization hash checks. - Models that pass regressions but degrade under long-tail inputs; we'll need periodic post-promotion audits.

anya: I'll draft a concise RFC: lifecycle diagram, state machine, API endpoints (ingest -> returns candidate_id, bench-status GET, bench webhook POST), bench SLAs, cost controls, and rollout recipe. Will add sample payloads and TTLs. Can volunteers for review ping me?

raj: I'll take a pass on the state machine and failure modes.

kevin: I'll mock the webhook schema in the intake service.

liz: I'll prepare the fast-probe golden set (50-100 items) and tokenizer checks.

bench-bot: Note: bench queue depth currently 6, median wait 1.4h.

anya: Thanks all — aiming to post RFC by EOD tomorrow.
